judgment.notes: All seven M applications are valid with the stated bindings. A001/M011 uses the finite index set {1,...,n}, real Lebesgue factors (sigma-finite by BG002–BG007) and decidable i≠j. A002/M017 uses the singleton subtype i=j, whose unique element exists because 1≤j≤n. Their product and composition give the actual coordinate map χ (BG024–BG025). A003/M006 has real complete normed codomain, G differentiable at every endpoint/interior point by N003 and BG014–BG018, and interval-integrable derivative by BG013/BG019; R>0 fixes orientation. A007/M003 has continuous H by N003/BG012–BG013, measurable opens and finite-on-compacts product measure by BG008–BG011, and compact support closure by BG027–BG029. A004/M016 has the measure-preserving measurable equivalence F002 and embedding BG026, with H∘χ exactly the original derivative section; this source requires no integrability premise. A005/M007 has the correct ordered product factors, s-finiteness BG005–BG007 and integrability from M003. A006/M013 uses B_j and T_j with their integrability from N002/F001. No E application occurs.

S001 legitimately specializes N002 at t0: t0/2<t0<3t0/2, so support, continuity and integrability apply; N003 supplies the exact derivative identity. S002 splits and then evaluates the singleton coordinate block, yielding χ and its explicit inverse. In S003, for arbitrary y the coordinate slice G is smooth and G' is the stated coordinate partial. At z=±R the inserted point is outside C, so both endpoint values vanish. M006 therefore gives zero oriented interval integral. Endpoint-null and support-extension steps, including global integrability of each slice, are verified in BG019–BG023. This works for every y, not only almost every y or y inside a box. S004 proves H continuous with compact support, so M003 gives product integrability. M016 followed by M007 and F003 gives zero whole-space derivative integral. S005 applies integral additivity to the pointwise N003 identity with integrable summands and rearranges its real scalar equality. No limit exchange or unproved integration-by-parts theorem is used. The n=1 empty factor is covered, n=0 has no index j, and m=0 causes no obstruction.

scope: Coverage is reviewer-reported; reading alone is not mathematical assessment.
